problem: Given that  $\text{Null}(A)={[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]\,:\,{x}_{2}\in R}$, find a basis for $\text{Null}(A).$
worked_solution:
Any vector in $\text{Null}(A)$ has the form

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Expanding, we get 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} \\ -3{x}_{2}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ \,\,1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, a basis for $\text{Null}(A)$ is

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ \,\,1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]}
$$

since it is a linearly independent set that generates $\text{Null}(A).$
